evals.prompt: Open the PR for this branch. It adds scheduled report exports: a schedule on a saved report, a queued run, and a control on the reports page.
evals.expected_output: A body with the ticket line, change type, a why-and-approach intro, grouped bullets, and a review focus.
expectations: Puts a linked ticket line at the top of the body
Titles it with the ticket key, a colon, and a concise sentence-case outcome
Opens with why the feature exists rather than restating the diff
Groups the bullets by surface, ordered by importance
Offers or includes a screenshot, because part of the change is visible
Ends with a review focus naming the part that carries risk
Uses natural domain language without class, method, column, or file references

evals.prompt: Title this PR. It adds retry handling for failed webhooks.
evals.expected_output: A ticket-prefixed title such as Add retry handling for failed webhooks, not a generic description of changed code.
expectations: Uses a concise title describing the outcome
Keeps the title scoped to the PR's single review objective
Uses domain language rather than implementation or file names
Does not use a generic title such as Changes to webhook code

evals.prompt: Open the PR for the export truncation fix. The export reused the list view's query, so it inherited the page size.
evals.expected_output: A body with numbered reproduction steps under their own header, followed by what changed and a review focus.
expectations: Leads with the overall behavioural or architectural change rather than the truncation symptom
Uses numbered reproduction steps, under their own header where a what-changed list follows
States the established mechanism rather than narrating a guess at it
Includes a link to the evidence that the defect exists, where one is available
Says what each change buys, not only that it was made
Points the review focus at the riskiest part rather than the one-line fix

evals.prompt: Write the PR body. A duplicate webhook incident prompted the work, but the branch introduces durable idempotent webhook processing across every delivery path.
evals.expected_output: A body led by the idempotent processing architecture, with the duplicate incident included only as supporting context.
expectations: Opens with the overall idempotent processing behavior and architecture
Describes the durable final state across delivery paths
Uses the duplicate incident only to support why the change was needed
Does not frame the PR primarily as a fix for one incident

evals.prompt: Open the PR for the extraction. It is a pure move, and it is the first of five changes.
evals.expected_output: A body that says what is mechanical, shows how that was established, and names the neighbouring changes.
expectations: States that the diff is a move with no behaviour change
Backs the claim, rather than only asserting it
Names what landed before and what depends on it, so the reviewer knows what they are not judging
Uses the repository or provider's stacked-PR tooling rather than representing the stack only in prose
Calls out any part that is not a pure move
Does not ask the reviewer to scrutinise the mechanical part

evals.prompt: Write the PR body for ABC-123. The title already contains ABC-123, so leave out its tracker link at https://tracker.example/browse/ABC-123.
evals.expected_output: A ticket line in the body anyway, with the reason.
expectations: Includes the ticket line at the top of the body, or of the template's context section
Explains that a ticket key in the title is plain text and gives no clickable route back
Does not omit the link on the strength of the title carrying the key
Keeps the key in the title as well

evals.prompt: Write the PR body. I asked you to leave two of the settings out because they are machine-specific, so mention that.
evals.expected_output: A body describing the final state, with the session's decisions left out.
expectations: Describes what the change now contains, not what was considered and dropped
Omits any deliberately-out-of-scope section
Appends no assistant session link
Says nothing about how the change was arrived at during the session
Offers to put the omissions in the ticket or a comment if they matter

evals.prompt: Open the PR. The repository has its own pull request template, with its own headings including a Testing one.
evals.expected_output: The repository's template filled in, with the ticket line inside its context section.
expectations: Uses the repository template's headings and vocabulary rather than the skill's own
Puts the ticket line in the template's context section
Writes no more than a bare acknowledgement under the forced Testing heading
Does not append the skill's own sections alongside the repository's
Does not treat previous PRs in the repository as the format to copy

evals.prompt: This PR renames a field across most of the module and adds one new rule. Write the review focus.
evals.expected_output: A focus line pointing at the new rule and clearing the rename.
expectations: Names the new rule as the thing to scrutinise
Says the rename is mechanical and needs no scrutiny
Backs the mechanical claim rather than only asserting it
Does not spread attention evenly across the whole diff

evals.prompt: Write the PR body, and mention that the whole suite passes and that I checked it locally against staging.
evals.expected_output: A body with no verification section, and the reason for leaving it out.
expectations: Leaves out suite counts, coverage numbers, and how it was verified locally
Keeps any evidence that the defect exists, such as a link to a failing run
Says why verification does not belong in the body
Allows the review focus to cite the existing suite where that clears a mechanical section

evals.prompt: Open one PR for the branch. It has a rename, a new abstraction, new rules, an API change, and a migration.
evals.expected_output: A split offered before opening, and the single PR opened with a risk-pointing review focus if the user still wants one.
expectations: Names the several review objectives the single PR would carry
Offers a concrete split, deferring the decomposition detail to write-plan
Opens the single PR if the user confirms, rather than refusing
Uses the review focus to point at the parts carrying the risk in that case

evals.prompt: Write the PR body for the cutover. Which implementation runs is selected by a config value.
evals.expected_output: A rollback line saying to set the config back, with no deploy needed.
expectations: States how the change is turned off without a deploy
Puts the rollback with the review focus at the end of the body
Writes no rollback line where reverting the commit is the whole answer
Says what the rollback does and does not take with it
